section_summary: This section records U.S. diplomatic reporting on Japanese merchant shipping from February 1940 through mid-1941, despite the file title's narrower date range. It covers restrictions on coastal shipping, Japanese control of trade around Canton, overseas routes, shipbuilding secrecy, vessel movements, and efforts to acquire ships. The later papers focus on confidential shipping intelligence and the growing difficulty of obtaining reliable information in Japan.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting notice of Shandong coast restrictions
subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy forwards information on the lifting of restrictions along part of the Shandong coast.
subfiles.summary: Morishima sends Hamilton an enclosure about coastal shipping restrictions.

subfiles.title: Notice of restrictions between Weihaiwei and Tsingtao
subfiles.about: Special anti-piracy restrictions applied to shipping between Weihaiwei and Tsingtao from February 15 to 24.
subfiles.summary: The notice describes the restricted coast and exempts the two ports.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Morishima's letter
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges the Embassy's report on coastal restrictions.
subfiles.summary: A brief letter thanks Morishima for the February 29 information.

subfiles.title: Japanese shipping activity at Canton and Whampoa
subfiles.about: Japanese military-flag transports dominate cargo and passenger traffic around Canton.
subfiles.summary: The consul reports that Japanese transports import consumer goods and export South China products while Whampoa remains closed to other powers. Japanese services have also gained passenger traffic at the expense of British and Portuguese operators. Continued control of Whampoa would leave other shipping at a disadvantage.

subfiles.title: New shipping reporting difficulties
subfiles.about: Japanese restrictions are reducing access to commercial ship construction and shipping data.
subfiles.summary: The consul describes the disappearance of published construction figures and other shipping news. He suspects material shortages have delayed the fleet program and plans to guard confidential sources.

subfiles.title: Request to transmit Kobe shipping reports confidentially
subfiles.about: A State Department officer requests guarded dissemination of Kobe shipping reports.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum proposes sending two reports to the Maritime Commission as confidential material.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Kobe shipping reports
subfiles.about: The State Department sends reports on Japanese shipping and reporting difficulties to the Maritime Commission.
subfiles.summary: Long requests confidential handling of the enclosed reports.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of confidential Kobe reports
subfiles.about: The Maritime Commission confirms receipt and guarded dissemination of the Kobe reports.
subfiles.summary: Land acknowledges the reports and agrees to restrict their circulation.

subfiles.title: Non-availability of commercial ship construction figures
subfiles.about: Japanese authorities have stopped providing commercial shipbuilding statistics.
subfiles.summary: Neither consular contacts nor Lloyd's can obtain current figures. A Lloyd's representative estimates construction is about 50 percent behind schedule.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Kobe shipbuilding despatch
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the Kobe report on unavailable ship construction figures.
subfiles.summary: A confidential copy of despatch 238 is enclosed.

subfiles.title: Cover despatch for Latin American shipping memorandum
subfiles.about: The consul forwards a memorandum on Japanese services to Latin America.
subfiles.summary: The cover despatch encloses Melbourne's requested memorandum.

subfiles.title: Japanese shipping services to Latin America
subfiles.about: Four Japanese steamship companies' passenger, mail, and cargo routes to Latin America are surveyed.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum details routes, schedules, and tonnage for Kawasaki Kisen, Nippon Yusen, Osaka Shosen, and Yamashita Kisen. It notes the recent growth of these services and the use of newer ships amid wartime hazards.

subfiles.title: Possible Japanese service to Central American Pacific ports
subfiles.about: A reported plan for regular Japanese calls at Central American ports is denied.
subfiles.summary: Frazer checks a local press report with a Japanese contact, who says it is unfounded. He recalls the line's earlier Pacific route and sees little likely southbound business.

subfiles.title: Japanese shipping agency report from Cartagena
subfiles.about: A Cartagena firm reportedly sought a Japanese shipping agency and received a discriminatory reply.
subfiles.summary: The report says the Japanese Legation would award the agency only to Germans or German sympathizers.

subfiles.title: Japanese ships ordered to use the Panama Canal
subfiles.about: The note points to a report that Japanese ships were ordered to use the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: It identifies the original despatch in another file.

subfiles.title: Proposed loan for Japanese shipping tonnage
subfiles.about: A Shanghai telegram concerns a proposed one-to-two-million-dollar credit for Japanese ship acquisition.
subfiles.summary: The note identifies the parties and points to the original telegram.

subfiles.title: Further reference to Japanese shipping loan
subfiles.about: The note refers to another Shanghai report on financing Japanese ship purchases.
subfiles.summary: It directs readers to the original report in a related file.

subfiles.title: Expiry clause in Japanese vessel purchase loan
subfiles.about: A telegram addresses an expiry-date clause in the proposed vessel-purchase loan.
subfiles.summary: The note summarizes the issue and gives the original telegram's file reference.

subfiles.title: New steamship service between Indochina and Japan
subfiles.about: Osaka Shosen has inaugurated a Haiphong-to-Japan service.
subfiles.summary: Flood reports the first ship's September 10 arrival in Haiphong.

subfiles.title: Japanese steamers withdrawn from American service
subfiles.from: A. W. Childs, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Two large Japanese steamers are reportedly withdrawn from service to the Americas.
subfiles.summary: Childs reports that the Brasil Maru and Argentina Maru are being recalled to Japan and replaced by smaller ships. He relays speculation that Japan wants its larger vessels nearer naval protection.

subfiles.title: Proposal to exchange merchant-vessel lists
subfiles.about: Japan proposes exchanging its 1940 merchant-steamer list for the latest U.S. merchant-vessel list.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy encloses two copies of the Japanese list and requests an exchange.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Commerce about vessel-list exchange
subfiles.about: State forwards Japan's 1940 vessel lists and seeks advice on a reply.
subfiles.summary: State asks Commerce how to respond and where to send any publications for transmission.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese vessel-list proposal
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Japan's proposed exchange of merchant-vessel lists.
subfiles.summary: The note confirms receipt of the lists and promises a later substantive response.

subfiles.title: Loan agreement for shipping tonnage
subfiles.about: The note points to a despatch enclosing a Japanese ship-purchase financing agreement.
subfiles.summary: It identifies the loan agreement and its original file.

subfiles.title: Credit to Japanese ship brokers
subfiles.about: The note connects the proposed loan to U.S. guidance on extending credit to Japanese firms.
subfiles.summary: It points to a Shanghai telegram and suggests informing the Americans involved.

subfiles.title: Instructions on proposed Shanghai shipping loan
subfiles.about: State requests fuller facts about a proposed loan for Japanese ship acquisition.
subfiles.summary: The Department distinguishes a loan from credit for a ship sale, asks about the source of two million dollars, and suggests showing the Americans a 1938 Commerce statement on credit to Japanese firms.

subfiles.title: German merchant vessels in Japan
subfiles.about: The note indexes a report listing merchant vessels at Japanese ports.
subfiles.summary: It names several ships and points to Grew's original telegram.

subfiles.title: Locations and movements of merchant vessels
subfiles.about: Grew reports vessels at Kobe, Yokohama, Dairen, and Osaka and recent ship sales or departures.
subfiles.summary: The telegram corrects vessel identifications and notes two ships sold under the Japanese flag.

subfiles.title: O.S.K. Japan–West Africa service
subfiles.about: The note indexes information on O.S.K.'s service from Japan to West Africa.
subfiles.summary: It lists ports on the route and attributes the information to M. Higashikuze.

subfiles.title: Commerce reply on merchant-vessel lists
subfiles.about: Commerce explains the U.S. publication schedule and asks for Japanese motor and sailing vessel lists.
subfiles.summary: The next U.S. list will be a 1941 calendar-year edition; Commerce will send two copies when published.

subfiles.title: State reply to Commerce on vessel lists
subfiles.about: State declines to request Japanese motor and sailing vessel lists reported unavailable.
subfiles.summary: Long says State conveyed Commerce's publication schedule to Japan and will pass along any later information about the missing lists.

subfiles.title: Update to Japan on U.S. merchant-vessel list
subfiles.about: State tells Japan when the next U.S. merchant-vessel list will be available.
subfiles.summary: Commerce received Japan's lists; State expects to forward two copies of the 1941 U.S. edition after publication.

subfiles.title: File charge slip
subfiles.about: A clerical slip records handling of an enclosure.
subfiles.summary: File-control markings only.

subfiles.title: Archival withdrawal notice
subfiles.about: A notice records removal of an access-restricted item.
subfiles.summary: The form identifies a withdrawn item and cites access restrictions.

subfiles.title: Secret instructions to Japanese ships
subfiles.about: The note points to allegations that Japanese consuls gave secret wartime instructions to ships.
subfiles.summary: It references the original Justice Department letter.

subfiles.title: Suggestion to inform Maritime Commission of Batiz report
subfiles.about: A State division proposes forwarding FBI intelligence on Bernardo Batiz's ship purchases.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum suggests sending the April 2 FBI letter to the Maritime Commission.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Bernardo and Rafael Batiz
subfiles.about: The FBI reports that Bernardo Batiz is negotiating to buy vessels allegedly for Japanese use.
subfiles.summary: A confidential source says the stated salt trade may conceal purchases for Japan's government. The letter identifies Batiz's brother Rafael and gives biographical details, while noting that the seller and Bernardo's New York address are unknown.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Batiz intelligence to Maritime Commission
subfiles.about: State forwards the FBI's Batiz ship-purchase report in strict confidence.
subfiles.summary: The note encloses the FBI letter for Commission use.

subfiles.title: Secret messages to Japanese shipmasters
subfiles.about: Naval intelligence reports secret consular messages to Japanese ships calling at Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum also notes missing noon-position reports and a consular appeal for calm.

subfiles.title: Photographs of the President Mitre
subfiles.about: The FBI sends photographs of the Japanese ship President Mitre.
subfiles.summary: The letter transmits photographs; pages 59–60 contain no readable OCR description.

subfiles.title: Cover letter for Japanese shipping memorandum
subfiles.about: The FBI sends confidential-source data on Japanese shipping activity.
subfiles.summary: Hoover encloses a memorandum and copies naval and military intelligence officers.

subfiles.title: Confidential-source memorandum on Japanese shipping
subfiles.about: A source alleges Japanese control of ship allocation and unusual cargo and provisioning patterns.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum claims Japan plans to concentrate vessels in the Pacific and avoid Panama Canal tolls. It also describes suspected transshipment of glycerin and tallow and increased provisioning by Japanese ships.

subfiles.title: FBI letter on Japanese tanker routes
subfiles.about: An FBI letter relays a shipping-press report on Japanese tankers avoiding the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: It says tankers are being directed to Pacific loading ports and notes increased loading at San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Routing note for FBI letter
subfiles.about: An internal note concerns copies of an FBI letter.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten instruction is only partly legible.

subfiles.title: Copy of FBI letter on Japanese tanker routes
subfiles.about: This is a clean copy of the tanker intelligence letter on page 63.
subfiles.summary: It reports Pacific-only tanker loading and increased activity at San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmission of tanker intelligence
subfiles.about: State forwards an April 18 official letter on Japanese tanker operations.
subfiles.summary: The covering letter sends the material in strict confidence.

subfiles.title: Extract on Japanese tanker operations
subfiles.about: An enclosure reproduces the substance of the FBI tanker report.
subfiles.summary: It describes Japan's shift toward Pacific oil loading and increased tanker calls at San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Maritime Commission acknowledgment of Batiz intelligence
subfiles.about: The Commission acknowledges the FBI report on Bernardo Batiz's possible vessel purchases.
subfiles.summary: Land says the intelligence will be considered if Batiz applies to buy an American vessel.

subfiles.title: Restrictions on Panama Canal use
subfiles.about: The note points to suggestions for excluding Axis shipping from the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: It directs readers to a related file; the source details are illegible.

subfiles.title: File charge slip
subfiles.about: A clerical slip records file handling.
subfiles.summary: File-control markings only.

subfiles.title: Launching of Japan–Seattle passenger ship
subfiles.about: The Miike Maru has been launched for Nippon Yusen's Japan–Seattle route.
subfiles.summary: Tower gives the April 12 launch date and the ship's planned passenger capacity, dimensions, engines, and speed.

subfiles.title: Rumored end of Japanese sailings to the United States
subfiles.about: The U.S. consul at Yokohama finds no evidence that Japanese sailings to U.S. ports will stop.
subfiles.summary: Lines continue advertising schedules and accepting reservations; no government reservation of all shipping space is known.

subfiles.title: File charge slip
subfiles.about: A clerical slip records file handling.
subfiles.summary: File-control markings only.

subfiles.title: Difficulties in reporting upon Japanese shipping
subfiles.about: Japanese secrecy rules are sharply reducing consular access to shipping information.
subfiles.summary: Sokobin describes declining publications, missing statistics, controls on launch reports, and official pressure on Japanese firms not to inform foreigners. Foreign contacts remain valuable but are leaving Japan or losing access. The consulate promises continued reporting and urges close attention by other posts.

subfiles.title: Commendation of Roy Melbourne's shipping reports
subfiles.about: State praises Melbourne's recent reports on Japanese shipping.
subfiles.summary: Three May 1941 reports receive excellent ratings, and Sokobin is asked to inform Melbourne.

subfiles.title: Fishing crews carried as merchant-ship crews
subfiles.about: The note references claims about Japanese fishing crews entering the United States under merchant-ship crew identities.
subfiles.summary: It summarizes the alleged crew substitutions and points to the original letter.
